name: Electric Charges and Fields
why: Gauss's law, dipole and field lines. Derivations here fit 3 and 5 mark slots.
rules: Pick the Gaussian surface by symmetry: sphere for a point or shell, cylinder for a line, pillbox for a sheet.
Line charge E = λ/(2πε₀r). Infinite sheet E = σ/(2ε₀). Inside a uniformly charged thin shell the field is zero.
Far from a dipole, the axial field is twice the equatorial field, and the equatorial field points opposite to p.
hook: Axial is Double.
trap: Using the point-charge 1/r² for a line charge. It falls as 1/r.

name: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
why: Capacitor combinations, energy, dielectrics. Short numericals, easy to lose on signs.
rules: Capacitors in series: 1/C adds. In parallel: C adds. This is the reverse of resistors.
Battery connected: V stays fixed. Battery disconnected: Q stays fixed. Decide which before using any formula.
Energy stored U = ½CV² = Q²/2C. A dielectric of constant K multiplies C by K.
hook: Battery on, V stays. Battery off, Q stays.
trap: After disconnecting the battery, a dielectric lowers V. It does not raise Q.

name: Current Electricity
why: Kirchhoff, metre bridge, potentiometer, internal resistance. Pure formula practice pays.
rules: Terminal voltage V = E − Ir. Power to the load is maximum when R = r.
Metre bridge at balance: R/S = l/(100 − l). A potentiometer draws no current at balance.
Kirchhoff: the junction rule is charge conservation and the loop rule is energy conservation. Fix a loop direction and keep it.
hook: Colour code: B B ROY of Great Britain has a Very Good Wife (Black, Brown, Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Violet, Grey, White).
trap: Flipping the sign of Ir when the cell is being charged.

name: Moving Charges and Magnetism
why: Biot-Savart, Ampere, force on charges, galvanometer conversion.
rules: Straight wire: thumb along the current, fingers curl along B. Loop: fingers along the current, thumb along B.
F = qv × B and r = mv/qB. The period T = 2πm/qB does not depend on speed.
Galvanometer to ammeter: a small shunt in parallel. To voltmeter: a large resistance in series.
hook: FBI for Fleming's left hand: Force thumb, B first finger, I second finger. APSV: Ammeter Parallel, Series Voltmeter.
trap: Applying the force rule to a negative charge without reversing the direction.

name: Magnetism and Matter
why: Mostly theory and definitions. Cheap marks for students who learn NCERT lines.
rules: Diamagnetic: weak repulsion, small negative susceptibility, independent of temperature. Paramagnetic: weak attraction, small positive susceptibility, χ ∝ 1/T (Curie). Ferromagnetic: strong attraction, large positive susceptibility.
Magnetic field lines form closed loops. Inside a bar magnet they run from S to N.
Torque on a magnetic dipole in a field: τ = mB sinθ.
hook: Dia = Denied (repelled). Para = Pulled weakly. Ferro = Fiercely pulled.
trap: Saying field lines start at N and end at S.

name: Electromagnetic Induction
why: Lenz's law, motional emf, inductance. Direction questions need a clear rule.
rules: Lenz's law: the induced current opposes the change in flux, not the flux itself.
emf = −dΦ/dt. Motional emf = Blv. Energy in an inductor U = ½LI².
Flux increasing: the induced field opposes it. Flux decreasing: the induced field supports it.
hook: Nature dislikes change.
trap: Writing 'opposes the flux' instead of 'opposes the change in flux'.

name: Alternating Current
why: Small weight, but LCR and resonance numericals reward a clean method.
rules: Vrms = V₀/√2 and Irms = I₀/√2. Meters read rms values.
Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²). At resonance X_L = X_C, Z = R, current is maximum and ω₀ = 1/√(LC).
Power factor cos φ = R/Z. A pure inductor or capacitor uses no average power.
Transformer: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. A step-up transformer raises voltage and lowers current.
hook: CIVIL: in a capacitor I leads V. In an inductor V leads I.
trap: Using peak values in average power formulas.

name: Electromagnetic Waves
why: Short chapter, mostly theory. Spectrum order and uses are quick marks.
rules: Displacement current I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt. It keeps Ampere's law consistent across a capacitor gap.
E and B are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, in phase, with E/B = c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀).
In order of increasing frequency: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma.
hook: Raging Martians Invaded Venus Using X-ray Guns.
trap: Listing the spectrum in wavelength order when the question asks for frequency order.

name: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments
why: Largest single chapter. Mirrors, lenses, prism, TIR, microscope and telescope.
rules: New Cartesian convention: distances from the pole, positive along the direction of the incident light.
Mirror: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. Lens: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f. Lens maker's formula: 1/f = (n − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂).
Total internal reflection needs light going from denser to rarer and an angle above the critical angle, sin C = 1/n.
Telescope in normal adjustment: M = f_o/f_e. A compound microscope has a short-focus objective.
hook: Mirror plus, Lens minus.
trap: Forgetting that u is negative for a real object.

name: Wave Optics
why: Young's double slit, single slit. A few formulas and a clear diagram.
rules: Fringe width β = λD/d. Bright at path difference nλ, dark at (n + ½)λ.
Single slit: the first minimum is at a sinθ = λ. The central maximum is twice as wide as the others.
Interference fringes are equal in width. Diffraction fringes are not.
hook: Interference is even. Diffraction has a fat middle.
trap: Swapping d (slit separation) with D (screen distance).

name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
why: Einstein's equation, stopping potential, de Broglie. Formula plus graph reading.
rules: Einstein: K_max = hν − φ. Stopping potential: eV₀ = K_max.
Frequency sets K_max. Intensity sets the photocurrent. Below the threshold frequency there is no emission at any intensity.
de Broglie: λ = h/p = h/√(2mK). For an electron through V volts, λ ≈ 12.27/√V Å.
hook: Frequency fixes energy. Intensity fixes count.
trap: Saying a brighter light gives faster photoelectrons.

name: Atoms
why: Bohr model, energy levels, spectral series. Quick numericals.
rules: Bohr: r ∝ n², v ∝ 1/n and E_n = −13.6/n² eV.
Series end at n = 1 (Lyman, ultraviolet), n = 2 (Balmer, visible) and n = 3 (Paschen, infrared).
1/λ = R(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), with R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹.
hook: Lyman UV, Balmer visible, Paschen infrared: lower levels 1, 2, 3.
trap: Using the upper level where the question gives the lower.

name: Nuclei
why: Binding energy, radioactivity, fission and fusion.
rules: Nuclear radius R = R₀A^(1/3), so density is the same for all nuclei.
1 u = 931.5 MeV/c². Binding energy = mass defect (in u) × 931.5 MeV.
Binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron. Light nuclei release energy by fusion and heavy ones by fission.
N = N₀(½)^(t/T) and the decay constant λ = 0.693/T.
hook: Light fuse, heavy split, iron is the middle.
trap: Mixing mass in kg and in u within one calculation.

name: Semiconductor Electronics
why: Seven marks for one chapter, mostly theory and diagrams. Good return for the time.
rules: N-type: pentavalent donor (P, As, Sb), electrons are the majority carriers. P-type: trivalent acceptor (B, Al, In), holes are the majority carriers.
Forward bias narrows the depletion layer. Reverse bias widens it.
A rectifier uses the one-way conduction of a diode. Half-wave uses one diode. Full-wave uses two or four.
hook: Pentavalent gives Negative carriers. Trivalent gives Positive holes.
trap: Drawing the diode symbol with the arrow reversed.

name: Solutions
why: Raoult's law, colligative properties, van't Hoff factor. Formula numericals.
rules: Raoult's law: p = p°x. Colligative properties depend on the number of particles, not their identity.
With the van't Hoff factor i: ΔT_f = iK_f m and π = iCRT. i > 1 for dissociation and i < 1 for association.
Positive deviation: weaker A–B attraction, ΔH_mix > 0, vapour pressure above ideal. Negative deviation is the opposite.
hook: Colligative = Count, not Character.
trap: Using masses where moles are needed.

name: Electrochemistry
why: Biggest unit. Nernst, Kohlrausch, Faraday's laws, cells.
rules: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode. Oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode.
Nernst at 298 K: E = E° − (0.059/n) log Q. ΔG° = −nFE°.
Λm = κ × 1000/M in S cm² mol⁻¹, with M in mol L⁻¹. Kohlrausch: Λ°m is the sum of the ion contributions.
Faraday: m = ZIt, and 1 F = 96,500 C.
hook: LEO says GER: Lose Electrons is Oxidation, Gain Electrons is Reduction. AN OX, RED CAT.
trap: Subtracting the wrong way round. Write cathode minus anode every time.

name: Chemical Kinetics
why: Order, rate constant, half-life, Arrhenius. Numericals reward practice.
rules: Order comes from experiment, not from the balanced equation.
Units of k: zero order mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹, first order s⁻¹, second order L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹.
First order: t½ = 0.693/k, independent of concentration, and k = (2.303/t) log([R]₀/[R]). Zero order: t½ = [R]₀/2k.
Arrhenius: k = Ae^(−Ea/RT) and log(k₂/k₁) = (Ea/2.303R)(1/T₁ − 1/T₂).
hook: First order: the half-life never changes.
trap: Reading the order off the coefficients of the equation.

name: The d- and f-Block Elements
why: Pure NCERT theory. Configurations, properties, KMnO4 and K2Cr2O7.
rules: Exceptions: Cr is 3d⁵4s¹ and Cu is 3d¹⁰4s¹.
The highest oxidation state in the 3d series is +7 for Mn. It rises up to Mn and then falls.
Colour comes from d–d transitions, so d⁰ and d¹⁰ ions such as Sc³⁺ and Zn²⁺ are colourless.
Lanthanoid contraction is a steady fall in size across the 4f series. It makes 4d and 5d elements of a group alike in size.
hook: Mn is the multi-valent king.
trap: Counting Zn, Cd and Hg as transition elements in a 'why' question.

name: Coordination Compounds
why: Naming, isomerism, hybridisation, crystal field theory.
rules: Name ligands in alphabetical order, then the metal. Anionic complexes end in -ate. Show the oxidation state in Roman numerals.
[Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is square planar (dsp², diamagnetic). [NiCl₄]²⁻ is tetrahedral (sp³, paramagnetic).
Strong-field ligands (CN⁻, CO, en, NH₃) pair electrons and give low spin. Halides and H₂O are weak field.
Isomerism to know: linkage, ionisation, hydrate, coordination, geometrical and optical.
hook: C and N donors are strong. Halides are weak.
trap: Ordering ligands alphabetically by prefix, such as di- or tri-. Ignore prefixes.

name: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
why: SN1 and SN2, name reactions, reasoning questions.
rules: SN1 order is 3° > 2° > 1° (carbocation stability) with racemisation. SN2 order is 1° > 2° > 3° with inversion.
Leaving-group ability I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > F⁻, so reactivity is RI > RBr > RCl.
Finkelstein gives iodides (NaI in dry acetone). Swarts gives fluorides (AgF, Hg₂F₂, SbF₃).
Chlorobenzene resists nucleophilic substitution: resonance gives the C–Cl bond partial double-bond character, and the carbon is sp².
hook: SN1 counts 3-2-1. SN2 counts 1-2-3.
trap: Treating a racemic product as a sign of SN2.

name: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
why: Preparation, properties, conversions, distinguishing tests.
rules: Lucas test (ZnCl₂/conc. HCl): 3° turns turbid at once, 2° in about 5 minutes and 1° does not at room temperature.
Phenol is more acidic than an alcohol because the phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance. Electron-withdrawing groups raise acidity.
Dehydration with conc. H₂SO₄: 443 K gives an alkene and 413 K gives an ether.
Williamson synthesis: sodium alkoxide plus a primary alkyl halide.
hook: Lower temperature, ether: two molecules join. Higher temperature, alkene.
trap: Using a tertiary halide in the Williamson synthesis. It eliminates.

name: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
why: Name reactions and conversions. Second-largest organic unit.
rules: Tollens' (silver mirror) and Fehling's (red precipitate, aliphatic aldehydes only) detect aldehydes. Iodoform detects CH₃CO– and CH₃CH(OH)–.
Rosenmund: acid chloride to aldehyde (H₂, Pd/BaSO₄). Stephen: nitrile to aldehyde (SnCl₂/HCl). Etard: toluene to benzaldehyde.
Aldol needs an α-hydrogen. Cannizzaro needs none (conc. NaOH).
Acid strength: carboxylic acid > phenol > alcohol. Electron-withdrawing groups raise acid strength.
hook: Aldol Asks for alpha-H. Cannizzaro Cannot have it.
trap: Saying that benzaldehyde gives Fehling's test.

name: Amines
why: Basicity order, tests, conversions, diazonium salts.
rules: In water: methylamines 2° > 1° > 3° > NH₃. Ethylamines 2° > 3° > 1° > NH₃. Aromatic amines are weaker than aliphatic ones.
Hinsberg: the 1° product dissolves in alkali, the 2° product does not, and 3° does not react. Carbylamine test: only primary amines (foul smell).
Gabriel phthalimide gives pure 1° aliphatic amines. Hoffmann bromamide gives an amine with one carbon fewer.
Diazonium salts: Sandmeyer (CuCl, CuBr, CuCN), Gattermann (Cu powder) and coupling to azo dyes.
hook: Methyl: 2-1-3. Ethyl: 2-3-1. Hoffmann hands over a carbon.
trap: Using the Gabriel synthesis for aromatic amines.

name: Biomolecules
why: Almost all NCERT theory. Among the cheapest marks in the paper.
rules: Sucrose is non-reducing because both anomeric carbons are tied up in the glycosidic bond. Maltose and lactose are reducing.
Starch is amylose plus amylopectin (α-links). Cellulose has β-links, which humans cannot digest.
DNA pairs: A=T with two hydrogen bonds and G≡C with three. RNA has uracil and ribose.
Deficiency: vitamin A night blindness, B₁ beri-beri, C scurvy, D rickets, K delayed clotting.
hook: A=T two, G≡C three.
trap: Stating that RNA contains thymine.

name: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
why: Diagram-heavy (embryo sac, anther, pollen, seed) with definition-style short answers on double fertilisation and post-fertilisation events.
rules: In double fertilisation one male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy) to form the zygote, and the other fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion) to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus.
The typical angiosperm embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate: three antipodals, two synergids, one egg cell and a large central cell with two polar nuclei.
The pollen grain exine is made of sporopollenin and has germ pores where sporopollenin is absent; the generative cell divides to form two male gametes.
hook: Seven cells but eight nuclei: the big central cell is the one carrying two nuclei.
trap: Writing the endosperm as diploid; it is triploid (3n) because it comes from the fusion of two polar nuclei with one male gamete, while the zygote is 2n.

name: Human Reproduction
why: Diagrams of the male and female reproductive systems and of gametogenesis, plus sequence-type answers on the menstrual cycle, fertilisation and implantation.
rules: One primary spermatocyte completes meiosis I to give two haploid secondary spermatocytes, which complete meiosis II to give four spermatids that change into sperms by spermiogenesis.
Primary oocytes formed in foetal life stay arrested in prophase I until puberty, and the secondary oocyte is arrested at metaphase II and completes meiosis II only after sperm entry.
A surge of LH near the middle of the menstrual cycle (about the 14th day of a 28-day cycle) triggers ovulation, and the ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum that secretes progesterone.
hook: LH acts on Leydig cells and FSH on Sertoli cells: L with L.
trap: Saying an ovum is released at ovulation; the cell released from the ovary is a secondary oocyte.

name: Reproductive Health
why: Mostly factual and definition-based: contraceptive methods, MTP, STIs and assisted reproductive technologies (ART) with easy recall marks.
rules: The WHO describes reproductive health as total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, namely physical, emotional, behavioural and social.

Copper-releasing IUDs such as CuT suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms, while hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.
In ZIFT a zygote or early embryo of up to 8 blastomeres is transferred into the fallopian tube, whereas an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres is transferred into the uterus (IUT).
hook: Saheli is the once-a-week non-steroidal pill: a weekly friend.
trap: Saying GIFT transfers a zygote; GIFT transfers the ovum (gamete) collected from a donor into the fallopian tube.

name: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
why: Highest-weight genetics chapter: crosses and ratio problems, pedigree analysis, sex determination and genetic disorders with both numericals and short answers.
rules: A monohybrid cross gives a 3:1 phenotypic and 1:2:1 genotypic ratio in F2, and a dihybrid cross gives a 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio.
In the ABO system the alleles IA and IB are codominant and i is recessive, giving six genotypes and four phenotypes, and any one person carries only two of the three alleles.
Sickle-cell anaemia is an autosome-linked recessive trait caused by a single base substitution (GAG to GTG) that replaces glutamic acid by valine at the sixth position of the beta-globin chain.
hook: Blood group AB shows both IA and IB products on the red cell: both alleles speak, none is quiet.
trap: Writing 3:1 for incomplete dominance; the F2 ratio is 1:2:1 for both phenotype and genotype because the F1 is intermediate.

name: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
why: Mix of experiment-based theory (Griffith, Hershey-Chase, Meselson-Stahl), process descriptions (replication, transcription, translation) and the lac operon diagram.
rules: In the Hershey-Chase experiment bacteriophages with radioactive 32P in DNA or 35S in protein infected E. coli, and only the radioactive phosphorus entered the bacteria, showing DNA is the genetic material.
AUG is the start codon and codes for methionine, and UAA, UAG and UGA are the three stop codons that code for no amino acid.
In the lac operon the i gene codes for the repressor, and lactose as the inducer binds the repressor so that the structural genes z, y and a are transcribed.
hook: P is in DNA and S is in protein: phosphorus labels DNA, sulphur labels protein.
trap: Mixing up the strands: the mRNA is complementary to the template strand and has the same sequence as the coding strand except that U replaces T.

name: Evolution
why: Theory and definitions (homologous and analogous organs, adaptive radiation, Darwin versus de Vries) plus a small Hardy-Weinberg calculation.
rules: Homologous organs such as the forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah and human show divergent evolution, whereas analogous organs such as the eyes of octopus and mammals show convergent evolution.
Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1 with p + q = 1, and allele frequency is disturbed by gene migration, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and natural selection.
S. L. Miller (1953) passed electric discharge through CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapour at 800 degrees C in a closed flask and obtained amino acids.
hook: Homologous: same blueprint, different job (divergent); analogous: same job, different blueprint (convergent).
trap: Treating 2pq as the frequency of an allele; p and q are allele frequencies and 2pq is the frequency of the heterozygote genotype.

name: Human Health and Disease
why: Fact-heavy theory: pathogens and diseases with causative organisms, immunity and antibody structure, AIDS, cancer and drugs, often as one-mark and two-mark recall.
rules: Plasmodium enters as sporozoites through the bite of a female Anopheles mosquito, and rupture of red blood cells releases haemozoin, which causes the recurring chill and high fever.
An antibody molecule has four peptide chains, two light chains and two heavy chains (H2L2), and IgE is the antibody linked with allergy.
HIV is a retrovirus with an RNA genome that makes viral DNA using reverse transcriptase and finally reduces the number of helper T-lymphocytes.
hook: Helper T cells are the conductor of the immune orchestra, so HIV silences the whole band.
trap: Calling antivenom or antitetanus serum active immunisation; ready-made antibodies give passive immunity, while vaccination gives active immunity.

name: Microbes in Human Welfare
why: Pure recall: microbe and product pairs, sewage treatment steps, biogas, biocontrol and biofertilisers, ideal for quick one-mark and two-mark questions.
rules: Citric acid is produced by Aspergillus niger, acetic acid by Acetobacter aceti, butyric acid by Clostridium butylicum and lactic acid by Lactobacillus.
Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) is the amount of oxygen needed by bacteria to oxidise all the organic matter in one litre of water, and the higher the BOD the more polluted the water.
Cyclosporin A is obtained from the fungus Trichoderma polysporum, streptokinase from Streptococcus and statins from the yeast Monascus purpureus.
hook: High BOD means thirsty microbes and dirty water.
trap: Saying biogas is formed aerobically; methanogens such as Methanobacterium produce it anaerobically and methane is its chief component.

name: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes
why: Process and diagram-based: restriction enzymes, vectors, PCR steps and gel electrophoresis, often with a flow or labelled-diagram question.
rules: EcoRI recognises the palindromic sequence 5'-GAATTC-3' and cuts between G and A on each strand, leaving sticky ends.
PCR has three steps, denaturation, annealing of primers and extension, and uses Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus because it stays active at the high temperature of denaturation.
In pBR322, insertion of foreign DNA at the BamHI site inactivates the tetracycline resistance gene (insertional inactivation), so recombinants are ampicillin-resistant but tetracycline-sensitive.
hook: DNA moves to the anode in a gel because DNA is negative, and the smaller pieces run farther.
trap: Thinking a DNA palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards on one strand; it reads the same 5' to 3' on both strands.

name: Biotechnology and its Applications
why: Application-based theory: Bt crops, RNAi, insulin, gene therapy, transgenic animals and biopiracy, mostly short explanations of how and why.
rules: Bt toxin from Bacillus thuringiensis is made as an inactive protoxin that becomes active in the alkaline gut of the insect, where it creates pores in midgut cells and kills the insect.
RNAi silences a specific mRNA through complementary double-stranded RNA, and it was used to protect tobacco roots from the nematode Meloidogyne incognita.
The first gene therapy (1990) treated a child with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency, but it is not a permanent cure because the corrected lymphocytes do not last.
hook: RNAi: a matching RNA strand acts like a lock on the mRNA message so it cannot be read.
trap: Saying mature insulin has three chains; proinsulin has A, B and C peptides, but mature insulin has only the A and B chains joined by disulphide bridges.

name: Organisms and Populations
why: Concept and graph-based: adaptations, population growth curves and equations, and the signs of population interactions.
rules: Gause's competitive exclusion principle states that two closely related species competing for the same limited resources cannot coexist indefinitely, and the competitively inferior one is eliminated.
Logistic growth follows dN/dt = rN[(K - N)/K] and gives a sigmoid curve that levels off at the carrying capacity K, while exponential growth follows dN/dt = rN and gives a J-shaped curve.
Commensalism is (+, 0) as in the orchid growing on a mango branch, mutualism is (+, +) as in lichens, and amensalism is (-, 0) as in the effect of Penicillium on bacteria.
hook: The cattle egret follows grazing cattle: the egret gains, the cattle are unaffected, so it is (+, 0).
trap: Treating amensalism as competition; in amensalism one species is harmed and the other is unaffected (-, 0), while in competition both are harmed (-, -).

name: Ecosystem
why: Definition and diagram-based: productivity, decomposition steps, energy flow and pyramids, with an occasional short numerical on the 10 per cent law.
rules: Net primary productivity is gross primary productivity minus respiratory losses (NPP = GPP - R).

Only about 10 per cent of the energy passes from one trophic level to the next (Lindeman's 10 per cent law), and plants capture only 2-10 per cent of the photosynthetically active radiation (PAR), which is less than 50 per cent of incident solar radiation.
In decomposition, humification forms dark, resistant humus, and mineralisation then releases inorganic nutrients into the soil.
hook: Humus is the dark, slow-to-decay nutrient store of the soil.
trap: Saying the pyramid of energy can be inverted; it is always upright, whereas the pyramid of biomass in the sea can be inverted.

name: Biodiversity and Conservation
why: Mostly theory recall: levels of biodiversity, patterns, causes of loss and conservation methods, with a species-area relationship graph or equation.
rules: The species-area relationship is a rectangular hyperbola whose log-log form is log S = log C + Z log A, and Z is generally 0.1 to 0.2 irrespective of the taxonomic group or region.
The Evil Quartet of biodiversity loss is habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions.
There are 34 biodiversity hotspots in the world, and three of them cover India: the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and the Himalaya.
hook: HOAC: Habitat, Over-exploitation, Alien species, Co-extinction.
trap: Saying species diversity increases from the equator towards the poles; it decreases from the equator towards the poles.
